title: §.XIV (4): With Flacius — flee Variata from ἀσπονδος hate of Reformed; tear seamless tunic
pass_a_gloss: (4.) Those who with the restless FLACIUS ILLYRICUS, called quarrelsome even by AUGUSTUS ELECTOR OF SAXONY himself (see the German Formula of Concord edited in the year just preceding, Appendix p. 119 at the end), and with the most bitter and all but raving Philip-Scourge: (of whom very many Theologians have complained, the Wittenbergers throughout the Acts of the Altenburg Colloquy — see the Author of the Ausführlicher Behauptung from p. 64 to 70, and together with the Wittenbergers the Leipzigers in an entire German Tract called Endlicher Bericht, copied at Wittenberg in Hans Lufft's type 1570, and Melanchthon himself, speaking calmly enough of the disturbances stirred meantime by Flacius, both in the Letter to Johann Mathesius standing among Melanchthon's Counsels & Judgments, Part 2, p. 257, and in a Letter written by his own hand to Ulrich Mordisius and lately exhibited as not yet edited from the Library of Adam Christoph Jacobi by Mr. Christian Jüncker in the Life of Luther p. 126, with these words among others: Gladly, he says, will I depart both from the painted actions of the Papists themselves and from Flacian Sycophancy whenever God shall will me to depart, whether dying or in exile. Dying, I will go to the School of the Son of God and the Heavenly Churches; in exile I will find, God helping, hospitality among better men than Flacius, who threatens to bring it about that I be driven from all Germany: I pray God that He rule and cover you. Farewell well, 4 November 1558.) — flee the Variata Augsburg Confession by Philip, especially because of the changed Tenth Article, from implacable (ἀσπόνδῳ) hatred toward the Reformed, worse than snake and dog; Yet they will not remember that this, as to the matter, is the same as the Invariata, the Naumburg Estates cited above being judges, Mentzer not denying it in the Prolegomena to the Exegesis of the A.C. p. m. 21 in the middle — that the Reformed neither seek nor can seek nor wish to seek any greater support for their opinion from that edition than from this; Nor does it become Christian Theologians, because of such Sycophancies, to tear and lacerate into parts Christ's seamless tunic, that is, Christ's beloved Church, most tenacious of Christian love by Christ's command.
pass_b_english: (4.) Those who side with restless Flacius Illyricus — called quarrelsome even by Elector Augustus of Saxony himself (German Formula of Concord, appendix p. 119 end, edition of the year just past) — and with that bitter, almost raving scourge of Philip. Many theologians complained of him: the Wittenbergers throughout the Altenburg Colloquy acts; the Ausführlicher Behauptung author, pp. 64–70; the Leipzigers with them in the whole German Endlicher Bericht (Wittenberg, Hans Lufft, 1570); and Melanchthon himself, speaking calmly enough of Flacius's storms — in the letter to Johann Mathesius (Counsels & Judgments II, p. 257) and in a hand-written letter to Ulrich Mordisius, lately printed as unpublished from Adam Christoph Jacobi's library by Christian Jüncker in the Life of Luther, p. 126 — including: "Gladly will I leave both the painted deeds of the Papists and Flacian sycophancy whenever God wills me to go, dying or in exile. Dying, I go to the Son of God's school and the heavenly churches; in exile, God helping, I will find lodging with better men than Flacius, who threatens to drive me from all Germany. I pray God to rule and cover you. Farewell, 4 November 1558."
From implacable (ἀσπόνδῳ) hatred of the Reformed — worse than snake or dog — they flee Philip's Variata Augsburg Confession, mainly because Article X was changed.

Yet they will not remember that, as to substance, it is the same as the Invariata: so judged the Naumburg estates already cited, and Mentzer does not deny it (Prolegomena to the Exegesis of the A.C., p. 21 mid) — that the Reformed neither seek nor can seek nor wish to seek any greater support for their view from one edition than from the other.
Nor does it become Christian theologians, for such sycophancies, to rip and tear Christ's seamless tunic — that is, his beloved church, most tenacious of Christian love by his command — into pieces.
source_text: (4.) Qui cum inquieto & ab ipso AUGUSTO, SAXONIAE ELECTORE, rixoso appellato (vid. Formul. Concord. Germanicam, anno proximè superiori editam Append. p. 119. in fine) FLACIO ILLYRICO, & acerbißimo, tantumque non delirante Philippo-Mastige: (de quo quam plurimi conquesti sunt Theologi, Wittenbergenses in Actis Colloquii Altenburgici passim, vid. Auctor der Aufführlicher Behauptung/ à pag. 64. ad 70. & cum Wittenbergensibus unà Lipsenses, Tractat. Germanico integro, Endlicher Bericht dictô, & Wittenbergae, literis Hans Luffts 1570. exscripto, Ipseque Melanchton, de turbis interim à Flacio excitatis, placidè satis locutus, cùm in Epistola ad Johann. Mathesium, inter Consilia & Judicia Melanchtonis exstante, Part. 2. pag. 257. tùm in Epistola, ejusdem manu exarata ad Ulricum Mordisium, &, ceu nondum edita, ex Bibliotheca Adami Christophori Jacobi, à Dn. Christiano Jünckero, in vita Lutheri p. 126. exhibita novissimè, hisce inter alia verbis: Libenter & ab ipsis Papistarum fucosis actionibus & Sycophantia Flaciana, discedam, inquit, quandocunque me Deus discedere volet, vel morientem, vel exulantem. Moriens, accedam ad Scholam Filii Dei & Coelestes Ecclesias; exulans inveniam, juvante Deo, hospitium apud meliores Flacio, qui minatur se effecturum, ut totâ Germania expellar: Oro Deum, ut vos regat atque tegat. Bene valete die 4. Novemb. 1558.) Variatam à Philippo Confessionem Augustanam, ob mutatum praecipuè Articulum Xmum, ex odio in Reformatos ἀσπόνδῳ, angue pejus ac cane refugiunt; Nec tamen meminisse volunt, hanc tàm cùm invariata, quà rem, eandem esse, judicibus Statibus Naumburgicis suprâ citatis, nec diffitente Mentzero Prolegom. in Exeges. A.C. p. m. 21. in med. quam nihil quicquam subsidii majoris ex ista, atq; ex hac, sententiae suae Reformatos vel petere, vel petere posse, vel petere velle; Nec decere Christianos Theologos propter ejusmodi Sycophantias, tunicam Christi inconsutilem, i. e. Ecclesiam Christi dilectam, dilectionisq; Christianae, jussu Christi, tenacissimam, in partes distrahere atque dilacerare.
